integration_feasibility: LOW for direct 3D medical-visualization tasks; MEDIUM for medical NLP inside the workflow. AntAngelMed is a text-only medical LLM -- it has no imaging/visualization head and cannot render, segment, or reason over 3D volumes. It is, however, well-suited as the medical-reasoning/service-task layer of an AirPMD/VidiFlow BPMN workflow: ingesting clinical notes, synthesizing capacity/occupancy reports, triaging bed/resource requests, and writing structured summaries that VidiCore/VidiFlow nodes consume. It is NOT a drop-in for imaging models (NV-Reason-CT, CT-CLIP, RadViLLA, NV-Generate-CT) whose outputs flow into your visualization graph. Practical path: pair AntAngelMed (or the local Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B + Qwen3-VL-Embedding-2B that the VidiFlow stack already uses) with NVIDIA 3D CT/VR models via Hugging Face transformers, and keep the heavyweight 103B AntAngelMed served through vLLM/SGLang or the antangelmed.tbox.cn API rather than loaded locally on Windows workstation hardware.
licensing_access_notes: AntAngelMed: Hugging Face cardData = Apache-2.0 (open, gated=false); README 'License' section says MIT (pointing at inclusionAI/Ling-V2 LICENCE) -- an inconsistency that must be resolved before any commercial use. Base architecture Ling-flash-2.0 is inclusionAI (MIT). Quantized variants (FP8, INT4) are the same Apache-2.0 family. NVIDIA 3D models: NV-Generate-MR explicitly NVIDIA OneWay Non-Commercial (academic-only); NV-Generate-CT/NV-Reason-CT open for research and development (no clinical-use claim -- 'not an autonomous diagnostic system or a cleared clinical product'). CT-CLIP/CT-RATE and MONAI models open for research. ModelScope mirrors the Chinese mainland audience (FP8 recommended there); HF is the primary canonical source. Note this is a newly released model (downloads 152 main / 107 FP8) with a Chinese README and a modelindex.dev model page; assume the release pipeline is still maturing.
